Exhibits a thorough understanding of Global CMC drug development, strong management skills, financial & research management practices and long term planning skills.
Excellent knowledge of various international regulatory and GMP requirements.
Must be goal oriented, able to work within a team environment, self-motivated and understand the business needs to meet timelines.

The Associate Director, Pricing is the International pricing lead for RINVOQ . The role sets RINVOQ's International pricing strategy and preserves the integrity of RINVOQ's price across its indications and markets. It turns pricing analysis into clear guidance, robust business cases and accurate financial assumptions, and supports Area and affiliate teams in achieving broad, timely and sustainable patient access that reflects the value of RINVOQ.

Pricing Strategy and Guidance:
Develop and maintain International pricing guidance for RINVOQ (price corridors and launch and re-pricing recommendations) in line with brand strategy, the Integrated Access Strategy (IAS) and corporate objectives.
Apply the Strategic Pricing Framework to define the price potential of new indications and formulations, and recommend indication and country launch sequencing that maximizes International value.
Develop contracting guidance and access models that address payer objections and affordability concerns while preserving the integrity of RINVOQ's price.
Monitor International pricing policy and competitor pricing, and flag risks and opportunities for RINVOQ early.
Business Cases and Pricing Governance:

Prepare and present business cases to the Executive Pricing Councils, with a clear recommendation, quantified financial impact, risks and mitigations.
PVTO and IRP Analysis:
Build and run price-volume trade-off (PVTO) analyses to evaluate price and access scenarios, breakeven volumes and the net revenue impact of pricing decisions at market and International level.
Assess International Reference Pricing (IRP) implications of every proposed price change, launch price and confidential agreement. Quantify cross-country spill-over and recommend the sequencing and price levels that preserve the integrity of RINVOQ's price across International markets.
Work with International Pricing analysts to design, run and interpret IRP, PVTO and launch-sequencing models, and turn the outputs into clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Plan and LRP:
Own the RINVOQ pricing assumptions in the annual Plan and Long Range Plan (LRP) process, including price evolution, launch timing, price erosion, IRP impact and risk and opportunity scenarios.
Collect, challenge and align pricing assumptions with Areas, affiliates and Finance, so that forecasts are consistent and explained.

Area and affiliates (primary partners): help key markets turn International pricing guidance into local outcomes, covering price potential, negotiation strategy, scenarios, fallback positions and objection handling for national and sub-national negotiations.

Working knowledge of International Reference Pricing and its impact on launch sequencing and price setting.
Ability to condense complex analysis into clear, concise recommendations for senior audiences. Excellent written and spoken English.

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules through Early-Stage Clinical Development.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific and leadership experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
For the Principal Research Scientist I position, we are seeking a highly motivated and experienced data scientist to provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), advanced analytics, and data automation within Analytical R&D. The successful candidate will partner closely with analytical scientists to frame high-value scientific questions, engineer and integrate complex analytical data, and develop fit-for-purpose models, visualizations, and digital solutions that accelerate data-driven decisions across pharmaceutical development.
The candidate will perform and direct data science and application-development activities, mentor and develop scientists, and provide leadership across multiple projects and initiatives. They will conceive, execute, and communicate multidisciplinary strategies; translate between analytical scientists, statisticians, data engineers, software and IT partners; and convert innovative concepts into sustainable, adopted solutions with measurable scientific and business impact.
This role requires a strong combination of data science depth, pharmaceutical or scientific domain awareness, product-oriented solution development, and collaborative leadership. The scientist will help shape the Analytical R&D data science strategy, establish reusable standards and best practices, coordinate initiatives across a global network, and foster productive partnerships with internal data science, statistics, information technology, and R&D organizations.
Responsibilities:
Provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, AI/ML, advanced analytics, visualization, and data automation initiatives supporting pharmaceutical development.
Consult with analytical scientists and project teams to define the scientific or business question, assess data readiness, select appropriate analytical approaches, and translate results into clear recommendations and decisions.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of data products and analytical solutions, including problem framing, data acquisition and integration, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development and validation, visualization, deployment, documentation, user adoption, and lifecycle support.
Develop and apply statistical, machine-learning, chemometric, and/or generative-AI methods to complex analytical data while ensuring approaches are scientifically sound, interpretable, reproducible, and fit for intended use.
Engineer, curate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from laboratory instruments, scientific systems, documents, and development workflows; improve data quality, traceability, accessibility, and reuse.

title: Fiber Delivery Technical Infrastructure Program Manager – Civil Deployment Manager, Global Connectivity Infrastructure Development
description:
Fiber Delivery Technical Infrastructure Program Manager – Civil Deployment Manager (FD-TIPM, Civil)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.
You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
How would you like to build the physical pathways that carry Fiber to the Cloud?
We are looking for a highly motivated, technically savvy Civil Deployment Manager (FD-TIPM) to deliver the underground and aerial infrastructure behind one of the world's largest and most complex networks. As a Civil DM, you will own metro and long-haul civil construction programs from start to finish. That includes conduit, duct bank, vault/handhole, directional bore, and aerial pathway builds that connect AWS data center campuses, regions, and network facilities.
Civil DMs manage highly technical, cost-efficient, fast-paced construction programs that keep pace with and enable AWS network growth. You will be accountable for schedule, cost, quality, and safety across multiple concurrent spans. You'll work with design engineers, permitting agencies, utilities, right-of-way owners, and construction contractors to turn route plans into delivered infrastructure.
Key Job Responsibilities
Own end-to-end delivery of civil fiber construction programs: route analysis, vendor selection, permitting, construction, as-builts, and turnover to fiber placement/splicing teams.
Develop and manage integrated program schedules. Identify the critical path, flag risks early, and drive mitigation to hit committed delivery dates.
Lead vendor RFQ/RFP processes, evaluate bids, and manage contractors against scope, cost, schedule, and quality expectations.
Manage budgets and approvals (CARs/PCRs), forecast spend, and control change orders.
Coordinate permitting and right-of-way with municipalities, DOTs, railroads, utilities, and private landowners.
Run risk registers and escalation paths, and write clear status updates for leadership. Own weekly program correspondence and MBR reporting.
Enforce construction quality and safety standards in the field. Conduct site walks, review inspection results, and make sure as-builts are accurate and complete.
Write technical documents (e.g., TORAs, route/vendor analyses, lessons learned) to drive decisions and scale best practices.
Drive continuous improvement in civil delivery processes, tools, and vendor performance.
Do you have deep experience in some or all of these disciplines?
Civil/underground utility construction management: conduit, duct bank, HDD/directional boring, trenching, vaults/handholes, aerial make-ready
OSP design and construction, including permitting and right-of-way acquisition
Contractor and vendor management on multi-million-dollar construction programs
Construction scheduling, cost control, and change management
Are you well versed in GIS (e.g., ArcGIS, Google Earth/KMZ), Salesforce, or Smartsheet?
Have you worked in QuickSight, Power BI, or Tableau to track program health and report to leadership?
If you have skills in each of these categories, or you have managed complex, interdependent construction programs from planning through closeout, this could be the role for you.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience
5+ years of construction or program management experience in civil, utility, telecom OSP, or heavy infrastructure

description:
About Amazon Web Services
Amazon Web Services (AWS) offers a broad set of global compute, storage, database, analytics, application, and deployment services that help organizations move faster, lower IT costs, and scale applications. These services are trusted by the largest enterprises and the hottest start-ups to power a wide variety of workloads — including web and mobile applications, data processing and warehousing, storage, archive, and many others.
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.
The Opportunity
For a decade, WorkSpaces has been exceptional at what it was designed to do: securely deliver a virtual desktop where a user logs in, applications load, work happens, the session ends. It is reactive by design—with no memory of what occurred, no understanding of intent, and no ability to act on the user's behalf. But work has changed. The modern enterprise now runs on three workforces: humans who set direction, AI agents that execute delegated work, and the systems that run the business. Non-human identities already outnumber human ones, yet no infrastructure layer governs all three within a single trust boundary. description:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.
Are you excited about defining a new category of software, AI teammates that help people learn and grow in the flow of their work? Do you want to shape how millions of professionals build skills, earn certifications, and get better at their jobs every day? Do you want direct and immediate impact on the way people and AI learn together?
As part of the AWS Training and Certification team, we are building AI learning teammates: agentic systems that don't just answer questions or hand out courses, but work alongside people, notice where they are getting stuck, and turn everyday tasks into moments of learning. These teammates bring the right guidance, practice, and credential right into the tools and tasks they already use. This is a new product space where the right experience is still being invented, and we are looking for a product leader who partners deeply with design to define it.
As a Senior Product Manager - Technical, External Services, you will partner with design and lead the development of AI learning teammates, owning the product vision, requirements, and roadmap from concept through go-to-market. You will champion the needs of learners and the organizations that train and certify them, and translate ambiguous, open-ended problems into clear product definitions and detailed business requirements documents. You will work hand-in-hand with design, engineering, science, learning scientists, and operational stakeholders to prioritize the roadmap and spearhead the definition of new capabilities.
This role sits where product, learning, and design meet. A great learning teammate is built on more than a strong model and solid systems. It depends on trust, on clear interaction patterns, and on how it feels to be coached while you work. You will co-own the end-to-end experience with design. That spans how a teammate joins a team, how it surfaces learning in the flow of work, how it recognizes mastery and guides someone toward certification, and how people stay in control of their own development.
The successful candidate must have exceptional problem solving skills, strong business judgment, and demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams. We are looking for a proven ability to execute both strategically and tactically, and someone who is excited to take on new, ambiguous projects that will be industry defining. This position requires a solid technical background, and the candidate should be customer-focused with a passion for learning, AI, agents, and the future of how skills are built.
AWS Training and Certification helps people and organizations build the cloud and AI skills they need to be successful, from foundational learning through role-based certifications recognized across the industry. As a member of this team, you'll support the development and management of AI-powered learning experiences that reach learners worldwide, including the agentic learning teammates that will define the next decade of how people grow their skills.
Key job responsibilities
Partner with design to define and own the end-to-end experience for AI learning teammates, from onboarding and interaction patterns to how learning is delivered in the flow of work.
Define product requirements and author business requirements documents that align engineering, design, science, learning scientists, and leadership around a shared vision for each capability.
Own the roadmap for one or more learning teammate product areas, making trade-off decisions across competing priorities, customer commitments, and technical investments.
Represent the product externally with enterprise customers, translating their workforce development and certification needs into product direction and measurable adoption goals.
Drive cross-team alignment to ensure teammate capabilities are composable and reusable across the learning portfolio, partnering with learning science and certification stakeholders to keep in-the-flow experiences grounded in proven learning principles.
A day in the life
You might start your morning in a design review, working through the interaction model for how a teammate offers a quick coaching moment the instant someone hits a task they haven't done before. By midday, you are reviewing skill-progression and certification-completion metrics and preparing a decision narrative for leadership on a proposed new capability. In the afternoon, you connect with learning scientists and engineering to pressure-test whether an in-the-flow learning experience is effective and feasible this quarter, then close out by refining requirements for the next capability and drafting a narrative that will guide customer-facing conversations.

About AWS
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. title: AirPods Analog Systems Engineer, Power
description:
The AirPods team is seeking an Analog Systems Engineer to help drive the design, development, and delivery of our next-generation products. As the power and battery management expert, you will sit at the center of cross-functional collaboration and technical decision-making. You will shape the fundamental power architectures that enable future audio experiences, guiding these critical subsystems from early concept through to final mass production.
In this role, you will own and assist with the end-to-end development of power and battery management subsystems. You will establish the subsystem architecture by performing tradeoff studies, tolerance analysis, simulations for power and signal integrity, and system modeling. Working closely with various cross-functional teams, you will guide component selection, assist with schematic and layout reviews, provide guidance on subsystem HW/FW integration, and define system specifications.
Beyond internal collaboration, you will partner directly with silicon vendors to drive the development, bring-up, and characterization of new PMICs and charger ICs. As designs mature, you will author hardware specifications, evaluate vendor datasheets, and support engineering prototyping. Throughout the development cycle, you will execute hands-on hardware and firmware debug, ultimately driving silicon, system, and manufacturing validation to ensure these subsystems scale successfully and reliably from engineering builds into mass production.
Minimum qualifications: BS/MS EE or equivalent
2+ years of experience in analog/mixed-signal hardware design
Deep understanding of various power mixed-signal building blocks: PMIC, DC-DC switching converter, LDO, charger, battery, PCM, ADC/DAC, temperature sensor, LED driver, ultra-low power design
Strong analog/mixed-signal analysis: tolerance analysis, simulations for power and signal integrity, timing sequencing, spec compliance, system modeling
Proficient in bench testing and equipment usage (oscilloscope, power supplies, electronic loads, DMM, etc.) for silicon and system validation
Excellent interpersonal and presentation skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to drive alignment across hardware, firmware, and silicon teams
Preferred qualifications: Experience in designing low-power, high volume consumer products
Experience leveraging AI tools and automation to accelerate design analysis, simulation, hardware characterization, and validation workflows
Experience with scripting languages such as Matlab and Python
Familiarity with SPICE-based simulation tools

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer - Matching, Apple Ads
description:
At Apple, we focus deeply on our customers’ experience. Apple Ads brings this same approach to advertising, helping people find exactly what they’re looking for and helping advertisers grow their businesses! Our technology powers ads and sponsorships across Apple Services, including the App Store, Apple News, and MLS Season Pass.
Everything we do is designed for trust, connection, and impact: We respect user privacy, integrate advertising thoughtfully into the experience, and deliver value for advertisers of all sizes—from small app developers to big, global brands. Because when advertising is done right, it benefits everyone!
You'll have the opportunity to develop models that improve our platform across the board, write production code to generate recommendations, work closely with business partners to help drive the development of new products as well as perform large scale and complex experiments to understand their effects. You've, or will develop a deep understanding of the ad network behavior, and will work with product management and business leadership to prioritize an innovation roadmap across multiple technical domains. You'll lead the conception, development, and delivery of state of the art capabilities that differentiate our products and are core to our business. You will work with complex problems in the ads retrieval space, provide solution that adhere to Apple’s privacy principles, review and contribute to state of the art in research, work with a variety of cross functional teams to ensure the feasibility and robustness of delivering new capabilities. This role will work closely with organizational partners and be expected to present findings across the organization.

Proven experience in NLP, information retrieval and search.
Ability to apply and implement research concepts, ultimately in production quality code.

title: Electrical Test Technician
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Electrical Test Technician to build the test infrastructure that lets Base ship new hardware and software with confidence. You’ll turn engineering designs into physical test benches and fixtures - from low-voltage signal harnesses to 240/480V power circuits - built to run around the clock.

 

As Base’s fleet grows, we need more test capacity, fast. Every station you build should be documented well enough that the next one goes up in days, not weeks - no re-engineering the fixture from scratch each time. You’ll work closely with engineering to know what to build, when to fabricate in-house, and when to send a part out.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and wire test benches and fixtures, from signal-level harnesses to 240/480V power circuits

 - Document every build so a station can be replicated quickly as we add capacity

 - Design and fabricate enclosures, mounting brackets, and racking systems built to run continuously, 24/7

 - Decide when to fabricate a part in-house and when to send it out, and make sure it’s built right either way

 - Keep test systems running and ready for engineering and automated testing, 24/7

 - Follow wiring schematics and match workmanship, safety, and inspection standards to the job - low-voltage signal work and 240/480V power work each have their own

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Hands-on experience wiring harnesses: cutting, stripping, labeling, and documenting the work so someone else can build it the same way

 - Experience building both a low-voltage signal harness from a schematic and a 240/480V power circuit

 - Experience designing or fabricating enclosures, mounting brackets, or racking systems

 - Comfort with power tools and fabrication equipment of all kinds

 - A team-first mentality and goal-oriented drive: you take on what’s needed and speak up about priorities rather than talking poorly about past teams

 - 1-3 years in electrical work, fabrication, motorsports, aerospace, or a similar hands-on technical role. Apprenticeships and trade training count

 


ABOUT THE TEAM

Base's Systems Integration team makes sure our batteries, inverters, and power systems work together as one reliable product in the real world. We own the development and test infrastructure the rest of engineering builds on: hardware-in-the-loop rigs, test benches and fixtures wired from signal-level harnesses to 240/480V power, and the software, CI pipelines, and data tools that run tests on them around the clock. Our job is to catch hardware and firmware issues before they reach a member's home, reproduce the ones that slip through in the lab, and give engineers the confidence to ship to the fleet fast. As the fleet grows, so does the need for test capacity, and the stations, tools, and tests this team builds set the pace for how quickly Base can ship new products.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

Are eager to learn how different parts of a complex operation connect

title: Manager, New Verticals - In-Store Data Platform Strategy & Operations
location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; Los Angeles, CA; Seattle, WA; Washington, DC; Chicago, IL; Tempe, AZ
description:
About the Team
New Verticals is an exciting team at DoorDash that is building and scaling new ways to delight our customers beyond restaurant delivery.
Our Central Operations team, part of New Verticals Strategy & Operations, is re-inventing how consumers shop grocery, convenience, alcohol and retail by making every store’s digital shelf match the physical shelf. We do this by onboarding new data sources that improve selection coverage, price accuracy, inventory accuracy, and the location data that helps Dashers find the store and the item. When these get better, consumers see what they want at the right price and receive it with fewer substitutions and refunds, Dashers shop and navigate faster, and merchants sell more. You will partner with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to build AI-enabled tooling, launch operational processes at scale, own metrics, and pull operational and product levers across our Grocery, Convenience, Alcohol and Retail businesses.
About the Role
We are looking to hire a Manager to own how we onboard new data sources, external and internal, onto our ecosystem. Externally, you will bring on inventory and syndicated data providers, CPG branded data, in-store robotics companies, and other software and technology partners. Internally, you will find new ways to leverage the data we already have. Together, these sources align the physical inventory of brick-and-mortar stores with the digital inventory. You will also explore how these assets could grow into an inventory-as-a-service solution. You will partner with Machine Learning, Engineering, Product, Data Science, and Commercial teams. You will sit in the Central Operations group within our New Verticals Strategy & Operations organization and report into a Senior Manager. You will manage a team of two.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Build from zero. You’ll take new data sources from ideation to production: sizing opportunities, structuring partnerships, running pilots, and scaling the winners across Convenience, Grocery, Alcohol, and Retail.
Think big. You’ll imagine what’s possible with new sources and new commercial models, including inventory as a service, and turn bold ideas into roadmaps.

title: Mechanical Engineer - Structural Simulation
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is the hardware and autonomy innovation engine at DoorDash. We design, build, and deploy custom robotics and autonomous delivery systems designed to operate safely, efficiently, and reliably in urban environments. We are currently kicking off development on our clean-sheet, next-generation robot platform—rethinking the mobility foundation from first principles to dramatically improve efficiency, payload dynamics, and service lifetime.
About the Role
As a Senior Structural Simulation Engineer (Level IC5) , you will be the foundational structural analysis authority for DoorDash Labs. You will own structural finite element analysis (FEA) across our next-generation robotic platform, working directly on core vehicle architecture—including chassis systems, suspension, closures, and sensor enclosures.
This role will be heavily focused on  future-forward designs starting from the early concept phase. In your first 90 days, you will drive our architectural exploration, define early vehicle load cases, and make strategic software ecosystem decisions (including standardizing and driving our commercial commitments around simulation tools). As development advances, you will shift from rapid concept modeling to production-intent structural refinement and physical test-to-simulation correlation.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will:
Build From Day Zero: Lead structural concept validation for a ground-up robotic platform, running high-velocity trade studies alongside chassis, suspension, and closures engineers.
Define Our Tooling & Workflows: Evaluate, select, and operationalize our primary CAE/FEA software tech stack (with an emphasis on ANSYS-based suites), negotiating capabilities and technical fit directly with vendors.
Establish Load Cases & Criteria: Formulate first-principles structural load cases, fatigue histories, stiffness benchmarks, and failure criteria for dynamic ground vehicle environments where little historical data exists.
Simulate Critical Vehicle Subsystems: Execute complex static, dynamic, modal, durability, and fatigue analyses on structural enclosures, cast and sheet-metal subframes, linkages, and moving mechanisms.
Drive Test-Simulation Correlation: Partner with physical test teams to correlate strain gauge, modal shaker, and dynamic field testing data back into simulation models to maximize predictive accuracy.
Influence Primary Architecture: Act as the math-first checkpoint for mechanical design decisions, steering CAD geometry toward optimized strength-to-weight ratios before parts hit prototype tooling.
We’re excited about you because:
Deep Structural Domain Expertise: You bring 7+ years of hands-on structural FEA and mechanical simulation experience (or an advanced degree—MS/PhD—with 4+ years) focused on structural integrity, stiffness, fatigue life, and dynamic loading.
Vehicle & Robotics Systems Background: You have a demonstrated track record analyzing moving vehicle architectures—such as automotive body-in-white (BIW), chassis frames, suspensions, structural battery enclosures, robotics, drones, or high-performance mobility platforms.
Software Mastery (ANSYS Preferred): You are an advanced user of industry-standard finite element solvers (ANSYS Mechanical/Workbench strongly preferred; Abaqus, OptiStruct/HyperMesh, or LS-DYNA considered) and understand solver theory, element formulations, and convergence troubleshooting.
First-Principles Mechanical Rigor: You possess strong mathematical and classical mechanics fundamentals; you don’t just hit "solve," but can gut-check stress distributions and shear loads with hand calculations.
Ambiguity & Green-Field Ownership: You thrive in early-stage product definitions where requirements are fluid, documentation is sparse, and decisions must be made quickly with high technical conviction.
Cross-Functional Communication: You clearly translate complex FEA stress tensors, fatigue curves, and deflection limits into actionable design guidance for mechanical design engineers and leadership.
Nice to Haves:
Prior experience establishing or transitioning a company’s CAE software stack from scratch.
Background in topology optimization, lightweighting cast/extruded aluminum structures, or composite material modeling.
Direct experience running durability and fatigue analysis on systems subject to rough-road, curb-strike, or cyclic vibrational abuse.
Working familiarity with CAD tools (e.g., NX, SolidWorks, or Creo) for rapid geometry defeature and design iteration.

location: San Francisco, CA ; Sunnyvale, CA; New York, NY
description:
About the Team
DoorDash’s mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about — helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses. At DoorDash, there are three audiences that are at the core of every decision we make - our Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers. The Research team has a direct link to uncover the unmet needs and pain points of each of these audiences. We bring their voices into the business in order to help set the strategic vision for all of DoorDash’s current and future products.
About the Role
We're looking for a Research Operations Manager to be the operational backbone of our research team, and a driving force behind DoorDash's commitment to customer obsession. Every great product decision starts with a real voice: a Dasher, a merchant, a customer. You'll own the systems, tools, vendors, and AI-powered processes that get those voices in front of the people building for them, faster and at greater scale. You'll also champion a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement, so the research practice keeps getting better along with our understanding of the people we serve. This is a high-impact role at the intersection of research, operations, and technology, built for someone who sees friction before it's surfaced and treats it as theirs to solve.
What You'll Do
Vendor & Procurement Management : Own the end-to-end lifecycle of research vendor relationships — from sourcing and evaluation through contract negotiation, onboarding, and ongoing performance review. You'll manage relationships with research tool providers, recruiting agencies, transcription and analysis services, and other third-party partners. You'll establish clear SLAs, hold vendors accountable, and continuously evaluate the market for better options.
Budget Management:  Own the research team's budget: track spend, forecast needs, manage purchase orders, and ensure resources are allocated to the highest-impact work. You'll build visibility and reporting so research leaders can make informed investment decisions, and you'll identify opportunities to optimize spend without sacrificing research quality.
Participant Recruiting Lead the strategy and execution of participant recruiting across studies — managing panels, recruiting vendors, and internal databases to ensure the team has access to the right participants at the right time. You'll develop screeners, coordinate scheduling, manage incentives and compliance, and build systems that make recruiting faster and less effort-intensive for researchers.
AI-Powered Research Tooling: Partner with researchers, engineering, design to evaluate, build, maintain, and scale AI-based tools that accelerate the research process, from automated synthesis and analysis pipelines to intelligent tagging, search, and knowledge management. You'll bring a practical, iterative approach: shipping tools that solve real problems, gathering feedback, and improving them over time.
Culture of Experimentation Be a visible champion for experimentation within the research team. This means creating the conditions (psychological safety, lightweight processes, shared frameworks) that make it easy for researchers to try new methods, tools, and approaches. You'll run retrospectives, document and share learnings, and help the team build an institutional memory around what works.
Operations & Scalability Design and maintain the operational infrastructure that keeps the research practice running smoothly: research repositories, documentation standards, onboarding materials, team rituals, and the tooling stack. As the team and its ambitions grow, you'll proactively identify bottlenecks and build solutions before they become problems. You will also partner across brands/regions to extend research operations infrastructure globally, adapting for local legal and market requirements.
What We're Looking For
7+ years of experience in research operations, UX operations, or a closely related role
Experience managing contractors or full-time employees, including setting priorities, providing feedback, supporting development, and ensuring delivery
Demonstrated experience managing research vendors and procurement processes
Experience owning and forecasting operational or project budgets
Experience with research repositories and recruiting platforms (UserTesting, Qualtrics, etc.)
Familiarity with prompt engineering or working with LLMs in a research or operations context. You don't need to code, but you're excited to build tools using AI and have strong intuitions about what to build and when
A systems thinker who can zoom out to see inefficiencies and zoom in to fix them
Strong communicator who can influence without authority and build trust across research, product, and engineering teams
High degree of self-direction. You spot problems before they're surfaced to you and move quickly to address them
Why This Role
Research Operations is often the difference between a research team that produces insights and one that produces impact. In this role, you'll have real ownership, a team that values your craft, and the opportunity to shape how a research practice operates at scale, including on the frontier of AI-assisted research.
Why You’ll Love Working at DoorDash
We are leaders – Leadership is not limited to our management team. It’s something everyone at DoorDash embraces and embodies.
We are operators – We believe the only way to predict the future is to build it. Creating solutions to lead our company and our industry is what we do on every project, every day.
We are learners – Everyone here is continually learning on the job, no matter if we’ve been in a role for one year or one minute. We are committed to learning and implementing what is best for our customers, merchants, and dashers.
We are one team – The magic of DoorDash is our people, together making our inspiring goals attainable and driving us to greater heights.

Smart Components North America (SCNA), a division of Illinois Tool Works (ITW) Automotive, manufactures innovative components for major automotive manufacturers. The Division IT Manager leads the Division’s IT function, delivering reliable, secure, and cost-effective technology services that support the business’s operational and strategic goals. Applying the ITW Business Model and 80/20 Front-to-Back process, this leader translates divisional business priorities into an actionable IT roadmap and leads its execution in alignment with Segment and enterprise IT standards, architecture, and governance.

The ideal candidate brings an open-minded, business-focused approach to technology, evaluating tools—including AI where appropriate—and recommending solutions that deliver the greatest value.

Apply ITW Toolbox methods, including 80/20 and Simplification, to analyze workflows, identify simplification and automation opportunities, and partner with end users to implement solutions.
Evaluate AI alongside traditional technology options when addressing business problems, recommending its use where it delivers clear value.
Demonstrate hands-on leadership by engaging directly with teams, systems, and processes as needed to remove roadblocks, accelerate delivery, and meet commitments.

Lead the deployment, monitoring, maintenance, upgrade, and support of the Division’s IT infrastructure, business applications, and plant-floor systems.

Manage IT projects from initiation through completion, including scope, schedule, budget, and stakeholder communication, and personally lead critical projects as needed.
Manage the lifecycle of IT hardware, software, and licenses.
Cybersecurity & Risk

Ensure AI tools used within the Division comply with ITW’s AI Framework and acceptable-use policies, including requirements for protecting company and customer data.
Support customer and regulatory security requirements.

Prepare business cases and cost-benefit analyses for IT investments, including AI.
Manage vendor relationships and negotiate contracts and service agreements within delegated authority.

Develop team capabilities in new areas, including AI, data, and cybersecurity.

This hands-on role plays a key part in improving safety, quality, efficiency, and productivity across the manufacturing process.
This position provides opportunities to develop advanced fixture design, fabrication, and troubleshooting expertise through hands-on training and mentorship, with a path toward increased technical responsibility within the Fixture/Foam Team.

Read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, sketches, and fabrication instructions to build accurate mechanical assemblies.
Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair mechanical and pneumatic systems, identifying root causes and implementing effective solutions.
Verify dimensions, alignment, fit, functionality, and workmanship throughout fabrication and assembly processes.
Identify and recommend design, fabrication, and process improvements to enhance safety, quality, efficiency, and reliability.
Support the design, development, and continuous improvement of manufacturing fixtures and production equipment.
Utilize hand tools, power tools, welding equipment, machining equipment, and other manufacturing technologies safely and effectively.
Learn and apply CNC routing, CAD software, and specialized foam fixture construction and troubleshooting techniques as required.
Develop and maintain fabrication, operating, maintenance, and project documentation.
Demonstrate initiative, ownership, attention to detail, and follow-through in completing assigned projects.
Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering, Production, Maintenance, and other departments to support operational objectives and continuous improvement.
Follow all applicable safety procedures, including the proper use of personal protective equipment and safe operation of machinery.
May be required to assist with spill response clean-up.
Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Education:
High school diploma or GED required.
Experience/Skills Required:
Minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience required.
Hands-on experience in the fabrication, assembly, modification, maintenance, or repair of mechanical equipment, structures, or components. Relevant professional, vocational, military, or significant personal project experience may be considered.
Practical welding and metal fabrication experience required, including the ability to produce quality welds.
Demonstrated ability to build, assemble, and repair mechanical equipment using hand tools, power tools, and fabrication equipment.
Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to understand, troubleshoot, and repair mechanical systems and components.
Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, sketches, and measurements.
Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and commitment to quality workmanship.
Self-motivated and dependable, with the ability to work independently and manage priorities effectively.

Basic computer skills, including the ability to document work, communicate effectively, and follow written instructions.
Ability to collaborate effectively with Manufacturing Engineering, Production, Maintenance, and other cross-functional teams.
Willingness to work in a hands-on role primarily on the manufacturing floor.

Experience with mechanical and pneumatic systems.

Job Description:
Loma Systems® is a premier manufacturer of inspection equipment used to identify contaminants and product defects in the food and pharmaceutical industries. We are part of Illinois Tool Works (ITW), a global Fortune 250 diversified industrial manufacturer of value-added consumables and speciality equipment with related service businesses. Operating under the core philosophies of 80/20 business processes, customer-back innovation and a decentralized entrepreneurial culture, the company focuses on solid growth, improving profitability and strong returns across its worldwide platforms and divisions. These divisions serve customers and markets around the globe, with significant presence in developed and emerging markets. ITW’s revenue totaled US$14.5 billion in 2021, with nearly 45,000 employees worldwide.
Production Team Leader
Location: Carol Stream, IL
The Production Team Leader is responsible for the day-to-day leadership, planning and execution of North American production. The role has full line-management responsibility for the production team and ensures equipment is built safely, meets quality requirements and is completed in line with agreed delivery commitments.
Combining visible shop-floor leadership with practical operational coordination, the position owns production scheduling, capacity planning, Kanban execution and daily production performance. The role works closely with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering / Quality, Supply Chain, Logistics and Customer Experience to maintain material and technical readiness, resolve constraints and improve production processes.
Responsibilities:
Team leadership and development
Lead, coach and develop the production team, setting clear expectations for safety, quality, delivery, productivity and workplace standards.
Manage daily work allocation, attendance, leave planning and performance reviews; address performance concerns with support from Human Resources and the Operations & Engineering Director.
Maintain regular shop-floor presence, build effective working relationships and involve employees in identifying and implementing improvements.
Maintain a team skills matrix and coordinate training and cross-training with Manufacturing Engineering and Engineering to improve capability, flexibility and coverage.
Production scheduling and capacity planning
Own and maintain a documented production schedule showing job priorities, assigned resources, expected effort, key milestones and completion dates.
Review available capacity against workload, employee skills, planned absence and material and engineering constraints; identify risks and propose practical recovery actions.
Assess requests to bring forward, defer or add orders, communicating achievable dates and the impact on existing commitments to Regional Sales Managers and Customer Experience.
Coordinate engineering release and technical readiness with the Engineering Team Leader and material availability with the Senior Buyer before confirming production plans.
Daily production flow and material readiness
Lead daily production meetings, to review progress, shortages, quality concerns, shipping priorities and actions with clear owners and due dates.
Manage daily production flow, work in progress and line clearance, keeping job status and operational records accurate and accessible.
Manage shop-floor Kanban execution, monitor stockouts and trigger replenishment in line with agreed processes; work with the Senior Buyer to review replenishment levels and support assigned purchasing activities.
Identify material shortages and overdue items early, communicate required dates and production impact to the Senior Buyer, and agree follow-up actions; monitor commitments for directly assigned purchase orders and escalate delivery risks promptly.
Coordinate production-team participation in cycle counts, the annual inventory count and inventory reconciliation, supporting the Senior Buyer, Logistics and Accounting.
Support cycle counts, the annual inventory count and inventory reconciliation in coordination with Supply Chain, Logistics and Accounting.
Safety quality and workplace standards
Maintain a safe, clean and organised production environment through daily housekeeping, 5S routines, clear work areas and appropriate part presentation.
Reinforce safe working practices, report hazards and near misses, and follow through on assigned corrective actions with the relevant safety and functional owners.
Ensure production follows approved drawings, work instructions, inspection and test requirements, and applicable quality and compliance procedures.
Contain and escalate production non-conformances promptly; work with Manufacturing Engineering / Quality and Engineering on investigation and corrective action.
Partner with the Manufacturing Engineer to improve assembly methods, layouts, standard work and production readiness for new or changed products; ensure agreed changes are implemented, understood and sustained.

Maintain and communicate production KPIs, including on-time delivery, lead time, assembly efficiency and stockouts, using accurate and consistent data.
Analyse performance gaps, identify contributing causes and implement or coordinate actions to improve results, escalating constraints outside the role’s authority.
Identify and deliver practical improvements using ITW principles, including 80/20, Front-to-Back and In-lining, with support from Manufacturing Engineering and the Business Improvement Coordinator.
Document key operating routines and improvement outcomes, establish backup coverage and demonstrate sustained benefits to safety, quality, delivery, cost or capacity.

Essential:
·         Demonstrated experience supervising or directly leading a manufacturing or assembly team, including work allocation, coaching and performance management.
·         Practical experience in production scheduling, capacity planning and coordinating material availability in a varied manufacturing environment.
·         Technical aptitude and ability to interpret engineering drawings, bills of materials and assembly documentation.
·         Experience using ERP / MRP systems and Microsoft Excel to maintain accurate operational records, schedules and performance information.
·         Ability to prioritise competing demands, identify delivery risks and communicate clear actions across functions.
·         A hands-on, organised and analytical approach, with evidence of implementing and sustaining improvements.
·         Working knowledge of manufacturing safety practices, quality controls and 5S principles.
Desirable:
Experience in capital equipment or mechanical / electrical equipment assembly, particularly for food, packaging or pharmaceutical applications.
Experience with Kanban, inventory control, shipping / receiving or production-related purchasing.
Familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics 365, ISO 9001 quality systems and ITW operating principles.
Relevant qualification in manufacturing, engineering or operations, or equivalent practical experience.

Illinois Tool Works Inc. StampTech Fasteners TM Division Description:
The ITW StampTech Fastener TM Division serves the major OEMs and Tier suppliers in the North American automotive market.  The division supplies stamped metal fasteners and engineered fastener assemblies that leverage our deep-draw stamping technologies.  The annual revenue for the division is approximately $160M.  Locations include Gallatin, TN, Lexington, KY & Naugatuck, CT.
The Division drives profitability by leveraging its innovative solutions and application engineering.  In addition to ITW’s industry leading research and development capabilities, StampTech Fasteners TM enhances our customers’ competitive advantage by maintaining advanced engineering and manufacturing facilities in North America, exchanging product, process, and benchmarking information with sister units worldwide and continually improving processes, material, and designs to ensure every product provides value and meets customer expectations.

Analyze progressive stamping dies to verify condition, proper clearances and identify issues for repairs, replacement or modifications
Ability to read blueprints, sketches and models of die components and tooling design
Calculates dimensions and clearances for proper die operation
Measures, marks, and scribes metal stock for machining.
Operates machine tools such as lathes, milling machine, and grinders to machine parts and verify conformance of machined parts to specifications.
Smooths flat and contours surfaces with equipment to fit and assemble parts together and into assemblies and mechanisms.
Connect sensors in dies to ensure quality.
Examines standard or previously used dies, tools, and jigs and fixtures, and recommends design modifications regarding construction and function of part.
Develop specifications and general descriptions for specialty tooling and draws or sketches design of product.
Operates overhead crane.
Maintains a safe, clean, and organized work environment at all times.

Maintains equipment including daily inspections.
Follow all rules, regulations and work processes set forth by the company.
Hold self-accountable to create and maintain a safe working environment.
Competently perform all tasks with a focus on safety within a fast-paced environment.
Contributes to team effort by focusing on continuous improvement and success for the entire team.
From time to time, personnel may be assigned other duties for the purpose of training, additional assistance or for other reasons as needed necessary by management.

Must have own tools.

Experience operating a forklift.
Ability to weld (MIG/TIG); preferred
Basic computer knowledge
Great organizational and time management abilities.
Attention to detail.

Lead the design of reusable data products that combine trusted data, business definitions, standardized metrics and KPIs, analytical models, lineage, governance, and semantic context.

Help move the organization from disconnected datasets and dashboards toward governed, reusable data products and trusted self-service analytics.
Partner with data science and AI teams to provide well-defined, governed data and business context for advanced analytics, machine learning, and GenAI-enabled solutions.
Recognize patterns across individual requests and convert them into common data products, architecture patterns, semantic models, standards, or reusable capabilities.
Lead cross-functional business and technical conversations, evaluate alternatives and tradeoffs, and create alignment across business, product, application, architecture, engineering, analytics, and AI teams.
Influence without direct authority, challenge assumptions constructively, and guide complex initiatives from problem definition through design, implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Communicate complex technical concepts in clear business language and translate business context into sufficient technical detail for delivery teams.
Provide architectural guidance and coaching to engineers, analysts, architects, and product teams, raising the quality and consistency of solutions across the organization.

Minimum 8 years of relevant experience in data and analytics architecture, data products, data warehousing, business intelligence, enterprise applications, or related disciplines.

Strong analytical judgment and the ability to independently navigate ambiguity, evaluate tradeoffs, and determine a path forward.
Ability to lead technical and business conversations, influence without authority, and build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to distill complex topics for different audiences.

The team operates at the earliest stages of innovation, working from unmet clinical needs through concept generation, derisking, and early development. By partnering closely with engineering, clinical, and business leaders, the Incubator helps shape Intuitive’s long-term growth by advancing transformational technologies that improve patient outcomes and expand access to care.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.
Essential Job Duties
Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.
Experience and Qualifications
MD or DO required; active clinical practice is valued but not required for candidates with substantial innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Must demonstrate at least one of the following experience profiles: (1) meaningful hands-on clinical practice or procedural care experience plus exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) strong venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, corporate strategy, or product strategy experience plus sufficient clinical fluency to evaluate medical needs and care pathways.
Ability to identify unmet clinical needs and convert observations into structured hypotheses, need statements, development plans, or investment theses.
Experience conducting clinician, patient, or stakeholder interviews and synthesizing voice-of-customer input into actionable product or strategy recommendations.
Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments where the path forward is uncertain and evidence must be built iteratively.
Strong cross-functional influence skills and ability to collaborate with engineering, clinical, regulatory, reimbursement, product, and business stakeholders.
Ability to evaluate clinical workflows, procedure economics, adoption barriers, competitive dynamics, and strategic implications for new technology platforms.
Clear executive communication skills, including crisp written synthesis, structured presentations, and the ability to explain complex clinical concepts to non-clinical audiences.
Curiosity, ownership mindset, and enthusiasm for building new technologies that can transform care delivery and improve patient outcomes.
Biodesign or equivalent needs-based innovation training preferred; experience in venture, startups, business development, product strategy, or corporate strategy strongly preferred.
Education and Training
MD or DO required.
Surgical or interventional specialty training preferred, but not required if the candidate demonstrates strong innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Clinical practice experience, residency/fellowship training, or comparable patient-care exposure preferred for candidates coming from a primarily clinical background.
Candidates with fewer years of clinical training or limited active practice experience may be considered if they bring substantial experience in early-stage innovation, venture-backed companies, medical technology strategy, product development, business development, or Biodesign.
Biodesign, MBA, MPH, MS, fellowship, or other formal training in innovation, product development, health economics, or business strategy is a plus.

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
This position requires a candidate with extensive experience supporting evidence generation strategy and execution of clinical studies. The Senior (Clinical Study Manager 4) role will develop and execute strategies for clinical and outcomes research studies to support regulatory approvals and key strategic evidence initiatives. As a member of the Clinical Affairs team, this role will be responsible for working with key stakeholders to design and develop clinical protocols and execute clinical studies (pre-market or post-market studies), with minimal supervision. The candidate will be required to work closely with clinical research associates (CRAs), clinical trial assistants (CTAs) and data management for the conduct and execution of the study, as well as with biostatisticians to review and interpret results of clinical studies, develop clinical study reports, or support the development of clinical publications. During trial execution, the CSM will drive the progress of the trial during site selection, site start-up and through enrollment and follow-up. The CSM will clearly provide guidance to the monitors about monitoring needs, and oversee compliance work on the study. The CSM will also take a leadership role in external communication with investigators and study teams. The ideal candidate will have experience previously managing multi-center, premarket studies in the United States (IDE for 510k or PMA submissions) and utilizing resources to research and scope research topics and to provide recommendations on clinical trial strategy. The candidate is also expected to have experience reviewing, interpreting and summarizing clinical literature.
Essential Job Duties
Responsible for leading assigned clinical research activities
Collaborate with internal stakeholders, investigators and KOLs to develop and review study design and concepts, prepare protocol and study outlines and subsequently driving identified initiatives
Responsible for the planning and execution of the clinical studies including site selection, analysis of potential patient recruitment and projections, creation of study related documents (protocols, case report forms, Informed consents, Clinical trial agreements, study reports), organizing IRB/EC submissions with follow-thorough to ensure successful progress
Responsible for independently conducting clinical studies on schedule and within budget while ensuring high quality and compliance
Perform on-site and remote site qualification visits, site initiation visits, interim monitoring visits and site close out visits.
Conduct clinical study monitoring to ensure regulatory and protocol compliance as well as overall data accuracy in accordance with the study clinical monitoring plan
Complete source data verification of clinical study data entered in an Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system or on a case report form at sites  or in data  listings to ensure regulatory and protocol compliance and overall accuracy
Liaise with sites and support in internal audit/inspection and ensure sponsor audit readiness
Liaise with external vendors and sites to negotiate contracts and budgets in collaboration with the legal team and management
Track study progress and provide regular status reports
Work closely with Biostatisticians on data analysis, interpretation and synthesis, in order to develop clinical study reports and /or support development of scientific publications
Track, process and manage site payments and support in study financial tracking by developing tracking tools as necessary
Organize and lead study meetings and other study activities as assigned
Mentor junior clinical study manager(s); provide guidance to CRAs and CTAs on monitoring and other study needs
Follow corporate (e.g., SOP’s) and regulatory requirements (e.g., GCP and US and OUS guidelines) and proactively manage studies, following such guidelines and requirements
Conduct literature searches and familiarize with literature to stay informed and abreast of relevant scientific/clinical knowledge and/or to determine evidence gaps
Critically appraise scientific literature and write clinical summaries to assist research and the development of clinical strategies and clinical investigational protocols
Review and revise Clinical Operations Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to assist Clinical Affairs leadership with continuous process improvement initiatives
For post-market research, collaborate with commercial groups (i.e., marketing) to understand market trends and utilize information to support of business goals through Clinical Affairs activities
For post-market research, provide scientific expertise to the Health Economics and Outcomes Research department for development of outcomes research analysis (including identification of appropriate diagnosis or reimbursement codes, selection of clinical outcomes for procedures of interest)
Work with clinical investigators to prepare manuscripts, abstracts, slide presentations, and poster presentations for scientific meetings and publications in collaboration with management
Support regulatory submission and approval of pre-market clinical studies and 510k(s), responsible for addressing regulatory body questions on clinical study design and results (e.g., protocol, ICF, eCRF, clinical study reports).
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
Previous experience implementing, supporting and managing medical device trials Significant knowledge of clinical and/or outcomes research study design
Strong experience in protocol and ICF development, writing clinical section(s) for regulatory submission
Strong experience in conducting literature searches, reviews and appraisal of the scientific data
Excellent ability to interact with physicians and other professionals inside and outside the company
Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice ICH/GCP and other applicable regulations, fundamental understanding of clinical research and monitoring requirements
Experience negotiating clinical research contracts and budgets
Must be able to work effectively on cross-functional teams
Must be able to travel 25-40% or depending on business requirements
Must be able to manage multiple projects and/or balance competing priorities
Strong communication, presentation and interpersonal skills with high attention to detail and organization
Ability to learn quickly, adapt to shifting requirements, and self-educate on different surgical specialties as applicable to clinical projects (“Self-starter attitude”)
Ability to lead project team consisting of CRAs and CTAs and support management with relevant study updates
Exhibits strong work ethic to help meet aggressive timelines or multiple projects when necessary with a problem-solving mindset
Required Education and Training
Advanced degree in a scientific or bioengineering field (M.S., Ph.D., or M.D.) with minimum 5+ years of clinical research experience; OR
Bachelor's degree in a scientific or bioengineering field with minimum 8+ years of clinical research experience; OR
Minimum of 10+ years of clinical research experience combined with relevant scientific or technical training.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Comfortable in a hospital environment, experience working with nurses and surgeons preferred
Understanding of statistics, statistical methods, and design of experiment is strongly preferred
Extensive experience with close and independent management of pre-market clinical studies (First Human Use or IDE) used for regulatory submissions
Strong track record of KOL management for multi-center studies
Experience working on global or multi-national studies

Our team designs and builds the embedded platform software infrastructure that supports critical
performance, safety and user-facing features of the da Vinci™ Surgical System, Intuitive’s flagship product.
We’re looking for a high energy, experienced embedded software engineer to take technical ownership
across our embedded platform software stack.
In this role, you will lead board bring-up initiatives, drive architectural decision for our next-generation platforms, and serve as a technical anchor for the team – mentoring junior engineers and collaborating cross-functionally with hardware, system software, and FPGA teams. You will own critical subsystems supporting video networking, UI display, and machine learning capabilities of Da Vinci 5 while driving improvements in robustness, reliability, manufacturability, and serviceability.
Essential Job Duties
Lead board bring-up activities for next generation-based platforms including bootloader configuration, BSP customization, peripheral driver integration and system validation – taking end-to-end ownership from initial power-on through production readiness.
Own development and drive the technical direction of embedded software for video networking, UI display, and machine learning applications on Linux-based systems – including architectural decisions, code review and performance optimization.
Design and own comprehensive test strategies to validate board functionality, peripheral interfaces, and system performance metrics – including defining acceptance criteria and driving resolution of complex hardware-software integration issues.
Partner with and technically guide hardware engineers to identify, root-cause and resolve board-level issues during early development phases – serving as the primary software interface for cross-functional hardware bring-up
Architect and lead the development of automated test frameworks for board validation and regression testing – establishing scalable infrastructure usable across multiple platform variants.
Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and hands-on debugging support – actively contributing to the growth of the team.
Author and maintain technical documentation including design specifications, bring-up procedures, and failure analysis reports in compliance with FDA-regulated development processes.
Required Education, Skills & Experience
Minimum of 8 years of related experience and a Bachelor's degree; or 6 years experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience
Expert-level proficiency in C and C++ for embedded systems development, including memory management, real-time constraints, and performance-critical code
Deep expertise in embedded Linux, including kernel internals, custom device driver development, BSP bring-up, and user space application development
Proficiency with embedded development and debugging tools including GDB, JTAG, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and cross-compilation toolchains – with a demonstrated ability to root cause complex hardware-software interactions
Proven hands-on experience with hardware interfaces and protocols (i2c, SPI, UART, USB, Ethernet, CAN) – including bring-up debugging, and driver development for each
Exceptional debugging and root-cause analysis skills, with a track record of resolving complex, multi-layer Hardware-FPGA-software integration failures in time-critical environments
Demonstrated ability to mentor and technically develop junior and mid-level engineers
Experience working in an FDA-regulated or other safety-critical development environment, including familiarity with design controls, traceability, and risk management processes
Effective written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and cross- functional team collaboration
Preferred Skills & Experience
Hands-on experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms (TX2/Xavier/Orin or similar) or comparable ARM-based SOCs in a production embedded environment
Hands-on experience with GPU acceleration (CUDA) and hardware-accelerated inference frameworks (TensorRT) in production embedded systems
Experience with QNX RTOS or other real-time operating systems in safety-critical applications.
Proficiency in Python and bash scripting for test automation, bootup design, and build system integration
Demonstrated experience in and comfort with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing

Strong experience with clinical study resources and budget management

Strong experience in developing study protocol and other study documents, conducting literature review, writing clinical section for regulatory submission

Excellent ability to interact with physicians and other professionals inside and outside the company

Strong communication, presentation  and interpersonal skills with high attention to detail and organization
Results-driven attitude and strong problem solving skills, consistently shows dedication or strong work-ethic to help meet aggressive timelines or multiple projects when necessary

description:
